name: Byron Carbone
life: “I still remember paying ten pennies a month into a tea tin.” Wednesday often includes a stop at the approach to Seabright Court, where Byron likes to watch the beach traffic thin enough for workers going the other way.
voice: I kept the fine in coins for years. The library wants a story hour instead.
appearance: Byron has a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth. Look for iron-gray waves. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a boxy denim jacket with a pocket notebook shaped by years of sitting on it. In conversation Byron looks toward the door whenever a name is called.
personality: Byron takes a rejection personally for a day and analytically on the second morning. Byron can be generous with a rival once the first night's sleep has intervened.
agenda: To give the library a useful story hour.
family: Mateo Park is Byron’s cousin. Byron picks the meeting place. Mateo sets the time to leave. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The split visit*, Mateo says, “I baked one cake to thank two people. They finally got to cut it while we were all in the same room.”
connections: Jorge Dias. They turn the unpaid fine into a reading the former pupil actually wants to finish.

reactions.situation: The former pupil offers to pay forty years of fines
reactions.response: Byron asks the library what it actually needs from the returning reader.

reactions.response: Byron asks which name they want to hear next time and uses it in the next ordinary introduction.
